detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with permission to search `index=oci`.
• Install and configure: Splunk Add-on for Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.
• Ensure `oci:audit` events are flowing (prerequisite UC: 4.7.1 when applicable).
• Map `oci` and field extractions per `docs/guides/aws.md`, `docs/guides/azure.md`, or `docs/guides/gcp.md` as appropriate.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Configure required cloud inputs per provider guide; index=oci sourcetype=oci:audit.
Expected sourcetype: `oci:audit`. Validate with:
```spl
index=oci sourcetype="oci:audit" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=oci sourcetype="oci:audit" eventName="com.oraclecloud.audit.UpdateConfiguration"
| table _time eventName identity.principalName resourceId
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
The search scopes `oci:audit` in `index=oci` and applies `eventName="com.oraclecloud.audit.UpdateConfiguration"` to surface `OCI Audit UpdateConfiguration`. Tune time range and alert threshold to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare result counts to the vendor console (CloudTrail Event history, Azure Activity Log, GCP Logs Explorer, or service-native UI). Spot-check `_time` and actor fields. Confirm CIM acceleration only after TA field mappings are verified.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_7_18_alert` with appropriate severity. Dashboard: Dashboard panel, alert, and weekly compliance report..
Failure modes: (1) empty results — verify TA input and index routing; (2) duplicate events — check S3/SQS duplication; (3) missing fields — upgrade `Splunk Add-on for Oracle Cloud Infrastructure` and review `props.conf` aliases; (4) alert fatigue — add CMDB/allow-list exclusions documented in knownFalsePositives.
